lesson: Unit 1 – Lesson 4: Skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing)
outcomes: I can listen for times of the day.
I can ask and answer When do you ...? in a game.
I can read about a day and write about my day.

mcq.q: What do Jasim and Yasir do in the morning?
o: They have art lessons at school.
mcq.why: Art lessons are in the morning.

mcq.q: Which sentence is from the text?
o: We don't play in the afternoon.
mcq.why: The text says We don't play in the afternoon.

mcq.q: In the Snap game, when do you say Snap!?
o: When the routine and the time match.

mcq.q: Which is the writing frame for your day?
o: I ... in the ... / I ... at night.
mcq.why: We write I ... in the ... and I ... at night.

mcq.q: Ask your partner about play. Which question is correct?
mcq.why: We ask When do you play?

mcq.q: Write about your day. Which sentence is correct?
o: I have breakfast in the morning.
I have breakfast at the morning.

o: We play tennis in the afternoon.
We play tennis at the afternoon.

mcq.q: Do Jasim and Yasir play in the afternoon? How do you know?
o: No. The text says We don't play in the afternoon.
No. They are at school at night.
mcq.why: The text tells us: We don't play in the afternoon.

mcq.q: Ali plays in the afternoon. How is his day different from Jasim and Yasir's day?
o: They don't play in the afternoon.
They play in the afternoon too.
mcq.why: Jasim and Yasir play in the evening, not the afternoon.

mcq.q: Why do we guess the answers before we listen?
o: To think about the words we will hear.
To finish fast and stop listening.
Because we don't need to listen.
mcq.why: Guessing helps us get ready to listen.
